title: Studying the evolution of exchange and dipolar interactions and spin correlation in vdW magnet CrCl3 across magnetic phases
authors: Prem B. Karki, Ayodimeji E. Aregbesola, Karishma Prasad, Jonathan Skeels, Avani Inamdar, Pooja Kalal, Jian Wang, Kapildeb Ambal*
abstract: Understanding quantum interactions in van der Waals magnets are critical to realizing their potential for next-generation magnetic, electronic, and spintronic applications. In this study, we investigated the evolution of exchange and dipole-dipole interactions in van der Waals magnet CrCl3 using multifrequency broadband (1-16 GHz) magnetic resonance on a bulk single-crystal CrCl3 sample. We found that the dipolar-broadened low-field resonance linewidth narrows due to exchange narrowing at higher resonance fields. Our findings show that the exchange interaction evolves exponentially as we lower the sample temperature from room temperature to 50 K. However, we found that the dipole-dipole interaction remains constant in the same temperature range. We have also detected the half-field magnetic resonance transition at room temperature, indicating a robust dipole-dipole interaction among spins. The measured inter-spin distance is 2.4(3) A at room temperature. The evolution of dipole interactions, the observation of half-field magnetic resonance, and the strong exchange interaction indicate short-range ordering/correlation in CrCl3 at temperatures far above the magnetic global ordering temperature. This study also demonstrates the significance and sensitivity of the multifrequency electron spin resonance technique for understanding quantum interactions and magnetic correlations in van der Waals magnetic materials.
summary: This work uses broadband magnetic resonance spectroscopy on CrCl3 to map the temperature evolution of magnetic interactions. By analyzing linewidth narrowing and resonance shifts, the authors distinguish between temperature-dependent exchange and relatively constant dipolar interactions. The findings confirm robust short-range magnetic correlations in the material, highlighting the technique's sensitivity for quantum magnetism studies.
main_problem: The study investigates how exchange and dipole-dipole interactions, along with spin correlations, evolve in the van der Waals magnet CrCl3 across different magnetic phases.
main_result: The research found that the exchange interaction evolves exponentially upon cooling, while the dipole-dipole interaction remains constant, indicating short-range magnetic ordering even far above the global ordering temperature.
method: The primary method involves multifrequency broadband (1-16 GHz) magnetic resonance measurements performed on a single-crystal CrCl3 sample, supplemented by structural characterization.
model_or_system: The physical system is CrCl3, a van der Waals magnet. Analysis utilizes the Anderson-Weiss model to interpret linewidth narrowing and employs the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) model to analyze temperature-dependent linewidth broadening.
key_observables: Magnetic resonance linewidth, exchange field ($B_{ex}$), dipolar field ($B_d$), half-field magnetic resonance transition, and the spin correlation length ($\xi$).
important_parameters: Temperature range (RT down to 50 K), microwave frequencies (1-16 GHz), and the measured inter-spin distance (2.4(3) A).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Anderson-Weiss theory for linewidth narrowing and the BKT model for analyzing the temperature dependence of correlations.
figures_summary: Figures show broadband magnetic resonance spectra across varying temperatures and orientations, illustrating linewidth narrowing due to exchange effects and the temperature dependence of correlation length fitted to the BKT model.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first characterizing the system using broadband magnetic resonance, then analyzing the temperature dependence of the exchange and dipole interactions, and finally using the BKT model to quantify the magnetic correlation length divergence near the phase transition.
why_interesting: The detailed spectroscopic measurements provide quantitative insights into the interplay between short-range magnetic correlations and long-range ordering in a tunable quantum magnetic material, which is crucial for designing spintronic devices.
